Abstract: Precision agriculture increasingly demands real-time, on-device inference for crop monitoring and yield estimation, yet deploying deep learning models on severely resource-constrained edge platforms remains a fundamental challenge. This paper presents DurianEdge-YOLO, a novel lightweight object detection framework specifically designed for real-time durian fruit (Durio zibethinus) detection on embedded devices. Unlike existing approaches that rely solely on backbone replacement for model compression, our method integrates four synergistic innovations applied to a YOLOv8n baseline: (1) a Lightweight Adaptive Attention Module (LAAM) that dynamically recalibrates spatial and channel features through a dual-branch depthwise mechanism with minimal parameter overhead, (2) an Efficient Adaptive Feature Fusion Neck (EAFFN) that replaces standard PAN/FPN concatenation with learned scalar-weighted multi-scale integration, (3) a unified two-stage compression pipeline combining structured L1-norm channel pruning with feature-level knowledge distillation from a YOLOv8m teacher, and (4) mixed-precision quantization-aware training (QAT) calibrated specifically for INT8 deployment on TensorRT and ONNX Runtime. We introduce DurianFruitDet-2024, a comprehensive benchmark dataset comprising [XX,XXX] images collected across real orchard conditions in Thailand and Malaysia, covering diverse illumination periods (morning, noon, evening), weather states, occlusion levels, viewpoints, distances, and camera devices. Ablation studies quantitatively validate the individual and combined contribution of each component. Our framework establishes a new state-of-the-art for durian detection on resource-constrained hardware and provides a replicable methodology for edge deployment of agricultural AI systems.
